healthcareSystem: Mixed public-private (government-subsidized for citizens, private for tourists)
qualityNotes: World-class private hospitals in Dubai and Abu Dhabi (Cleveland Clinic Abu Dhabi, Mediclinic). Expensive without insurance. English widely spoken in medical facilities.
pharmacyHours: Most pharmacies open 9am-10pm, many 24/7 in Dubai and Abu Dhabi malls and hospitals
pharmacyTips: Pharmacies are well-stocked and modern. Pharmacists speak English. Some medications that are OTC elsewhere are controlled in the UAE — check before traveling.
prescriptionRules: Many medications require a prescription. The UAE has strict drug control laws — some common medications from other countries are banned or controlled.

restrictedMeds.name: Sleeping pills (some)
restrictedMeds.note: Many benzodiazepines and sleep aids are controlled — check specific medication

restrictedMeds.name: ADHD medications (Adderall, Ritalin)
restrictedMeds.note: Requires advance approval from UAE Ministry of Health

restrictedMeds.name: Some antidepressants
restrictedMeds.note: Some SSRIs and psychiatric medications require documentation

restrictedMeds.name: CBD/cannabis products
restrictedMeds.note: Zero tolerance — even trace amounts can lead to imprisonment

bringDocumentation: CRITICAL: Get approval from the UAE Ministry of Health BEFORE traveling if you take controlled medications. Bring a doctor's letter, original prescription, and medications in original packaging. The UAE has a zero-tolerance drug policy — violations can result in imprisonment.

travelInsurance.requiredNote: Health insurance is mandatory for all visitors to Abu Dhabi. Dubai requires insurance for visa holders. Most tourist visas now include basic health coverage.
travelInsurance.tips: Private healthcare in Dubai/Abu Dhabi is extremely expensive. A simple ER visit can cost $500+, hospital stays $1,000+/night. Comprehensive travel insurance is essential.

required: Yellow Fever (if arriving from endemic area)
vaccinations.notes: No special vaccinations required for most travelers. Yellow fever certificate required only if arriving from an endemic country.

waterNotes: Tap water is desalinated and technically safe to drink, though most residents and visitors prefer bottled water for taste. Bottled water is cheap and widely available.
foodSafetyTips: Excellent food safety standards in restaurants and hotels. Street food is generally safe. Be cautious with food from very informal vendors in older souks during summer heat.
medicalTourismNote: Dubai and Abu Dhabi are growing medical tourism hubs, especially for dental work, cosmetic surgery, and orthopedics.
sources: UAE Ministry of Health and Prevention
metaDescription: Complete health & medication guide for traveling to the UAE (Dubai & Abu Dhabi). Strict drug laws, banned medications, mandatory health insurance, emergency numbers, and pharmacy tips.

hospitals.name: Cleveland Clinic Abu Dhabi
hospitals.notes: World-class hospital. Part of Cleveland Clinic network.

hospitals.name: Mediclinic City Hospital
hospitals.notes: Close to Burj Khalifa and Dubai Mall. Emergency department.

pharmacyPhrases.english: I need medicine for a headache

dentalCare.availability: Excellent dental care in Dubai and Abu Dhabi. Modern clinics with latest technology.
dentalCare.costRange: AED 200-500 ($55-135) for consultation; AED 500-1,500 ($135-410) for fillings
dentalCare.notes: Dental care in the UAE is expensive but high quality. Many dentists trained internationally.
dentalCare.emergencyTip: Hospital emergency departments handle dental emergencies. Many dental clinics open evenings and weekends.

mentalHealth.englishTherapists: Widely available in Dubai and Abu Dhabi. English is commonly used in healthcare.
mentalHealth.notes: Mental health services are growing in the UAE. Private therapy: AED 500-1,000 per session.

accessibilityInfo.overview: UAE has good accessibility in modern areas. Dubai Metro is one of the most accessible transit systems globally.
accessibilityInfo.transport: Dubai Metro is fully wheelchair accessible. RTA provides accessible taxis. Most malls and attractions are accessible.
accessibilityInfo.tips: Desert safaris and older souks may have limited accessibility. Modern attractions like Dubai Mall and Burj Khalifa are wheelchair accessible.

covidStatus.entryRequirements: No COVID testing or vaccination requirements.
covidStatus.notes: UAE removed all COVID restrictions. Heat-related illness is a bigger health concern.

insuranceClaimProcess: UAE hospitals are accustomed to insurance. Many offer direct billing. Keep all receipts and medical reports in English (standard). Dubai Health Authority regulates healthcare pricing.
